\n <div><h2>Как действуют гормоны</:
How hormones act

Protein hormones (insulin, ACTH) cannot cross the membrane; they act through receptors on the cell surface and second messengers. Steroid hormones (cortisol, sex hormones) and thyroid hormones enter the cell and change gene activity — so they act more slowly but for longer.

Feedback

Almost all hormonal systems rely on negative feedback: the product inhibits its own release, like a thermostat.

\n <div><h2>Два уровня защиты</h2>\:
Two levels of defense

Innate immunity works immediately and in the same way against everything: skin and mucous membranes, phagocytes (neutrophils, macrophages), inflammation, interferons. Adaptive immunity is specific and has memory: B lymphocytes release antibodies, killer T cells destroy infected cells, helper T cells coordinate the response.

Vaccination

A vaccine creates memory cells without the disease. The first vaccine (against smallpox) was introduced by Edward Jenner in 1796; the theory of phagocytosis was proposed by Ilya Mechnikov (Nobel Prize, 1908).

<b>Улитка в развёрнутом виде.</b> Основн: The cochlea unrolled. The basilar membrane is narrow and stiff at the base (left), wide and floppy at the apex (right). There the stereocilia of the hair cells bend: the inner hair cells (yellow) send the signal to the nerve, the outer ones (green) tune the membrane and amplify faint sounds. This is how the ear splits sound into frequencies, the way a prism splits light.

\n <div><h2>Громкость и частота</h2:
Loudness and frequency

The ear codes frequency by the place on the membrane (high frequencies near the base) and, for low sounds, by the rhythm of impulses. Loudness is coded by the number of active fibers and their firing rate. The range of loudness is enormous: from 0 dB (threshold of hearing) to 120–130 dB (threshold of pain).

Why hearing declines

Hair cells do not regenerate. Loud music and noise damage them; the cells at the base suffer first — so high frequencies are lost first.

\n <div><h2>Как кожа держит темпера:
How the skin controls temperature

Thermoregulation is controlled by the hypothalamus. In the cold, skin blood vessels constrict, shivering and “goose bumps” appear; in the heat, the vessels dilate and sweating begins (humans have 2–4 million sweat glands).

Where the signal goes

From the receptors, along sensory nerves to the spinal cord, then via the dorsal columns and the medial lemniscus to the thalamus and the postcentral gyrus (areas 3, 1, 2). Pain and temperature travel along the spinothalamic tract.

<b>Эритроциты</b> — двояковогнутые диски: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) are biconcave discs 7–8 µm across, without a nucleus and packed with hemoglobin. They carry oxygen from the lungs to the tissues and some of the CO₂ back. There are 4–5 million in 1 µL of blood; they live ~120 days and are destroyed in the spleen and liver; every second the bone marrow releases ~2 million new ones. Their flexible shape lets them squeeze through capillaries narrower than themselves.
<b>Лейкоциты</b> — белые клетки с ядром,: White blood cells (leukocytes) are nucleated cells, 4–9 thousand per 1 µL. Neutrophils (up to 70%, segmented nucleus) are the first to arrive at an infection and eat bacteria. Lymphocytes (large round nucleus) are the B and T cells of immune memory. Monocytes (bean-shaped nucleus) move into the tissues and become macrophages. Eosinophils fight parasites and take part in allergy; basophils release histamine. White blood cells can leave a vessel through its wall.
<b>Тромбоциты</b> — безъядерные пластинк: Platelets (thrombocytes) are anucleate plates 2–3 µm across, fragments of giant bone marrow cells. There are 150–400 thousand in 1 µL; they live 7–10 days. When a vessel is damaged, they stick to the wound, become activated (put out projections) and clump together into a plug.
<b>Плазма</b> — 55% объёма крови: на 90%: Plasma makes up 55% of blood volume: it is 90% water and 7–8% proteins (albumins keep water in the vessels, globulins include antibodies, fibrinogen is for clotting), plus glucose, salts, hormones and metabolic products. An adult has about 5 L of blood — 7–8% of body weight.
<b>1. Спазм сосуда.</b> Повреждённая сте: 1. Vascular spasm. The damaged wall contracts reflexively — bleeding decreases. Blood flows out of the wound.

<b>3. Свёртывание.</b> Каскад факторов с: 3. Coagulation. A cascade of clotting factors (calcium and vitamin K are required) converts prothrombin into thrombin, and thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into fibrin threads. The fibrin mesh entangles the plug and red blood cells — a clot forms. The whole process takes 3–8 minutes.
<b>4. Ретракция и заживление.</b> Сгусто: 4. Retraction and healing. The clot contracts, pulling the edges of the wound together. Then the cells of the wall repair it, and the fibrin is dissolved (fibrinolysis). In hemophilia one of the factors is missing — the blood barely clots.

  • Defense: white blood cells, antibodies, clotting.
  • Regulation: temperature, pH, water and salt balance.

History

Blood groups were discovered by Karl Landsteiner in 1900 (Nobel Prize, 1930), and the Rh factor by him and Wiener in 1940. Only after that did transfusion become safe.

<b>Менструация (дни 1–5).</b> Уровни эст: Menstruation (days 1–5). Estrogen and progesterone levels are low, and the functional layer of the endometrium is shed. The pituitary begins to secrete FSH — follicles grow in the ovary.
<b>Фолликулярная фаза.</b> Под действием: Follicular phase. Under the influence of FSH the dominant follicle matures and secretes more and more estrogen — the endometrium thickens.
<b>Овуляция (~14-й день).</b> Пик эстрог: Ovulation (~day 14). The estrogen peak triggers a sharp surge of LH from the pituitary — the follicle ruptures and the egg is released into the tube. It remains viable for about a day.
<b>Лютеиновая фаза.</b> На месте фоллику: Luteal phase. In place of the follicle the corpus luteum forms and secretes progesterone — the endometrium becomes soft and rich in blood vessels. If there is no fertilization, after ~12 days the corpus luteum regresses, hormone levels fall and a new cycle begins.
Как устроены половые системы, как гормон: How the reproductive systems are built, how pituitary and ovarian hormones set the 28-day cycle, and what happens to a new life in its first week.
\n <div><h2>Половые клетки</h2><p>Я:
Germ cells

The egg (~0.1 mm) is the largest cell in the body; the sperm (~0.05 mm including the tail) is one of the smallest. Both are formed by meiosis and carry 23 chromosomes each. The sex of the child is determined by the sperm: one with an X chromosome gives a girl (XX), one with a Y gives a boy (XY).

Hormonal regulation

Hypothalamus (GnRH) → pituitary (FSH and LH) → ovaries or testes (estrogens, progesterone, testosterone), which act back on the hypothalamus and pituitary through feedback.

Около 28 дней, за которые гипофиз и яичн: The roughly 28 days during which the pituitary and ovaries prepare an egg and the uterine lining for a possible pregnancy — day by day, with hormones, the follicle and the endometrium.
<b>Роза.</b> Аромат — смесь десятков мол: Rose. The scent is a mixture of dozens of molecules (phenylethyl alcohol, geraniol, citronellol…). Each one excites several types of receptors, and the brain recognizes the smell by the pattern of active glomeruli.
<b>Кофе</b> — больше 800 летучих веществ: Coffee contains more than 800 volatile compounds. The pattern is broader and more complex: this is how the brain tells “coffee” apart from its individual components.
<b>Апельсин</b> — в основном лимонен. Др: Orange is mostly limonene. A different set of receptors means a different pattern of glomeruli in the bulb.
<b>Дым.</b> Запах гари обрабатывается бы: Smoke. The smell of burning is processed quickly and triggers alarm: the olfactory pathway goes straight to the amygdala and the paleocortex, bypassing the thalamus.
<b>Сладкое</b> — сахара и некоторые белк: Sweet — sugars and some proteins and sweeteners. The T1R2+T1R3 receptor on type II cells. The signal: “energy here”.
<b>Умами</b> — вкус глутамата (бульон, с: Umami is the taste of glutamate (broth, cheese, tomatoes, soy sauce); receptor T1R1+T1R3. The signal: “protein here”. It was described by the Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda in 1908.
<b>Горькое</b> — около 25 разных рецепто: Bitter — about 25 different T2R receptors. The highest sensitivity of all tastes: many poisons are bitter. The signal: “careful”.
<b>Кислое</b> — ионы водорода (кислоты),: Sour — hydrogen ions (acids), type III cells. A signal of unripe or spoiled food.
<b>Солёное</b> — ионы натрия проходят че: Salty — sodium ions pass through ENaC sodium channels. Needed for water and salt balance.
<b>Обоняние.</b> В своде носовой полости: Smell. In the roof of the nasal cavity lies the olfactory epithelium (~5 cm²) with ~10 million receptor neurons. Each neuron carries one receptor type out of ~400; all neurons of the same type send their axons through the ethmoid bone to the same glomerulus of the olfactory bulb. An odor is coded by the pattern of active glomeruli. Olfactory neurons live 1–2 months and are constantly replaced. Choose a smell.
<b>Язык</b> покрыт сосочками: грибовидны: The tongue is covered with papillae: fungiform (all over the surface), circumvallate (large, in a V near the root) and foliate (along the sides). The taste papillae contain 2,000–8,000 taste buds. The “tongue map” with a sweet zone at the tip and a bitter zone at the root is a myth: all five tastes are sensed by the whole surface.
<b>Вкусовая почка</b> — «бочонок» из 50–: A taste bud is a “barrel” of 50–100 cells with a pore at the top. Cells of different types respond to different tastes and pass the signal to fibers of the facial, glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves → brainstem → thalamus → gustatory cortex of the insula. The cells live 10–14 days. Choose a taste.
Два химических чувства: нос различает ты: Two chemical senses: the nose tells thousands of smells apart by the pattern of hundreds of receptors, and the tongue senses five basic tastes. Together they give what we call the flavor of food.
\n <div><h2>Вкус еды — это в основн:
The flavor of food is mostly smell

When we chew, volatile substances rise from the oropharynx into the nose (retronasal smell). That is why food seems tasteless when you have a cold: the tongue still senses sweet and salty, but the “aroma” disappears.

What makes smell special

It is the only sense whose signals reach the cortex without passing through the thalamus — directly to the paleocortex, the amygdala and the entorhinal cortex. That is why smells are so strongly linked to emotions and memories. For discovering the olfactory receptors, Richard Axel and Linda Buck received the 2004 Nobel Prize.

<b>Рёбра</b> — 12 пар. Первые 7 пар (ист: Ribs — 12 pairs. The first 7 pairs (true ribs) attach by cartilage directly to the sternum, pairs 8–10 (false ribs) attach to the cartilage of the rib above, and pairs 11–12 (floating ribs) end freely in the abdominal muscles. At the back, each rib articulates with a thoracic vertebra and rotates upward during inhalation, like a bucket handle.
<b>Грудина</b> — плоская кость спереди:: The sternum is a flat bone at the front: the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process. The clavicles attach to the manubrium and connect the arm to the axial skeleton. The sternum contains red bone marrow — it is used for marrow biopsies.
<b>Грудной отдел позвоночника</b> — 12 п: The thoracic spine consists of 12 vertebrae with articular facets for the ribs. Together with the ribs and sternum it forms the rib cage — a protective frame for the heart and lungs.
<b>Межрёберные мышцы</b>: наружные подни: The intercostal muscles: the external ones raise the ribs (inhalation), the internal ones lower them (forced exhalation). From below, the thoracic cavity is closed by the dome of the diaphragm. On the outside, the chest is covered by the pectoralis major and minor.
<b>Средостение</b> — пространство между: The mediastinum is the space between the lungs: the heart in its pericardial sac, the aorta and the venae cavae, the trachea and main bronchi, the esophagus, the thymus, nerves and the thoracic duct. Each lung lies in its own pleural sac.
<b>Железистая ткань</b> состоит из 15–20: The glandular tissue consists of 15–20 lobes radiating from the nipple like the spokes of a wheel. Each lobe is divided into lobules, and the lobules into tiny sacs (alveoli), where milk is produced during breastfeeding.
<b>Млечные протоки</b> собирают молоко о: The milk ducts collect milk from the lobules and open onto the nipple through 15–20 openings. Just before the nipple they widen slightly.
<b>Сосок</b> и окружающая его пигментиро: The nipple and the pigmented areola around it contain smooth muscle fibers and Montgomery glands, which secrete a protective fluid.
<b>Жировая ткань</b> определяет форму и: Adipose tissue determines the shape and size of the breast — which is why size has nothing to do with the amount of milk. Cooper’s ligaments — thin connective-tissue bands running from the skin to the fascia of the pectoral muscle — support the gland. The breast has no muscles of its own: it lies on the pectoralis major.
<b>Лимфа</b> от молочной железы оттекает: Lymph from the breast drains mainly (~75%) to the axillary lymph nodes, and also to the nodes along the sternum. That is why a doctor always checks the armpit during an examination.
<b>Грудная клетка</b> — каркас из 12 пар: The rib cage is a frame of 12 pairs of ribs, the sternum and 12 thoracic vertebrae. It protects the heart, lungs and great vessels, supports the muscles of the shoulder girdle and, together with the diaphragm, works as a pump for breathing. Click a part.
<b>Молочная железа</b> (разрез сбоку). О: The breast (side section). It lies on the pectoralis major and consists of glandular tissue (15–20 lobes with ducts), adipose tissue and connective-tissue ligaments. People of both sexes have mammary glands, but in women they develop at puberty under the influence of estrogens and progesterone. Click a part.
<b>Лактация.</b> После родов гормон гипо: Lactation. After childbirth the pituitary hormone prolactin makes the alveolar cells produce milk (glowing lobules). Click “Nursing”.
<b>Рефлекс выделения молока.</b> Сосание: The milk ejection reflex. Suckling stimulates receptors in the nipple → a signal travels along nerves to the hypothalamus → the posterior pituitary releases oxytocin → the muscle cells around the alveoli contract, and milk flows along the ducts to the nipple. Suckling also sustains prolactin production. The first milk — colostrum — is especially rich in antibodies.
Костный каркас, который защищает сердце: The bony frame that protects the heart and lungs and helps us breathe, and how the breast is built — from lobules to ducts and the hormones of breastfeeding.
\n <div><h2>Здоровье груди</h2><p>Е:
Breast health

Monthly self-examination and check-ups with a doctor help detect lumps in time. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women (it also occurs in men); at an early stage it responds well to treatment. After age 40, regular mammography — an X-ray examination of the breast — is recommended.

Hormones

Estrogens are responsible for the growth of the ducts, progesterone for the development of the lobules, prolactin for milk production and oxytocin for milk ejection.

<b>1. Возбуждение.</b> Сигнал из мозга (: 1. Excitement. A signal from the brain (thoughts, images, touch) travels down the spinal cord to the sacral parasympathetic center (S2–S4). Parasympathetic fibers dilate the arteries of the pelvic organs, and blood rushes to them (vasocongestion). Heart rate, blood pressure and breathing begin to rise, and muscle tone increases. Duration: from minutes to hours.
<b>2. Плато.</b> Возбуждение достигает в: 2. Plateau. Arousal reaches a high, stable level. Blood filling of the tissues is at its maximum, heart rate is 100–150 bpm, breathing is rapid, and the skin may redden (the “sex flush”). The pelvic floor muscles are tense.
<b>3. Оргазм</b> — самая короткая фаза (: 3. Orgasm is the shortest phase (seconds). Now the sympathetic center (T10–L2) takes the lead: rhythmic contractions of the pelvic floor muscles (driven by the somatic S2–S4 nerves) at intervals of ~0.8 s, and a peak in heart rate (up to 110–180) and blood pressure. The pituitary releases oxytocin, and the brain’s reward system (dopamine) is active.
<b>4. Разрешение.</b> Кровь оттекает, пу: 4. Resolution. Blood drains away, and heart rate, blood pressure and breathing return to baseline. Prolactin is released — it contributes to the feeling of satiety and relaxation. Men enter a refractory period (from minutes to hours) during which another response is impossible; women may not have one and can have repeated orgasms.
<b>Цикл полового ответа</b> — последоват: The sexual response cycle is the sequence of physiological changes described by William Masters and Virginia Johnson (1966): excitement → plateau → orgasm → resolution. It is controlled by the brain (cortex, limbic system, hypothalamus) and the autonomic nervous system: the parasympathetic division (green, sacral) is responsible for blood inflow, and the sympathetic division (red, thoracolumbar) for orgasm and emission.
<b>Круговая модель Розмари Бэссон</b> (2: Rosemary Basson’s circular model (2000). For many people, especially in long-term relationships, desire does not always come first: a person may start from a willingness to be intimate, and desire appears only in response to stimuli and arousal. Satisfaction (emotional and physical) sustains the motivation for the next cycle. The model complements Masters and Johnson’s linear scheme.
Как мозг, вегетативная нервная система,: How the brain, the autonomic nervous system, blood vessels and hormones work together to carry the body through the four phases of the sexual response — from excitement to resolution.
\n <div><h2>Нервы и гормоны</h2><ul:
Nerves and hormones

  • Brain: the cortex (thoughts, images), the limbic system and the hypothalamus initiate and regulate the response; dopamine is linked to desire and reward.
  • Parasympathetic system (pelvic nerves from S2–S4): vasodilation and blood inflow.
  • Sympathetic system (T10–L2): smooth muscle contractions and orgasm.
  • Oxytocin: muscle contractions and a feeling of closeness; prolactin: relaxation and refractoriness; testosterone and estrogens support libido in both sexes.

Important

The duration of the phases and the shape of the curve vary greatly between people and situations — the “norms” here are broad. Persistent difficulties with desire, arousal or orgasm are a reason to see a doctor (a urologist, gynecologist or sexologist): the cause is often hormones, blood vessels, medications or stress.

<b>Гипоталамус</b> (медиальная преоптиче: The hypothalamus (the medial preoptic area and other nuclei) is the main “center” of sexual behavior. It is sensitive to sex hormones and, via the pituitary (LH, FSH), controls the activity of the gonads.
<b>Дофаминовая система вознаграждения</b: The dopamine reward system: ventral tegmental area of the midbrain → nucleus accumbens → prefrontal cortex. Dopamine creates motivation, “wanting” and anticipation. The same system works during eating and other pleasant events.
<b>Миндалина</b> оценивает эмоциональную: The amygdala assesses emotional significance: attractiveness, safety or threat. Fear and anxiety suppress desire.
<b>Префронтальная кора</b> отвечает за к: The prefrontal cortex is responsible for control, weighing consequences, social norms and decisions. It can both strengthen and inhibit desire — which is why human behavior is not determined by hormones alone.
<b>Половые железы</b> выделяют тестостер: The gonads secrete testosterone and estrogens. Testosterone supports libido in both men and women (in women it is produced in smaller amounts by the ovaries and adrenal glands). Estrogens and progesterone influence desire at different phases of the cycle.
<b>Влюблённость (влечение к конкретному: Being in love (attraction to a specific person). According to the model of anthropologist Helen Fisher, this is a separate system: lots of dopamine and norepinephrine (euphoria, energy, sleeplessness, thinking “only about him/her”), while serotonin is reduced — hence the obsessive thoughts. It usually lasts from a few months to 2–3 years.
<b>Привязанность.</b> В долгих отношения: Attachment. In long-term relationships, oxytocin and vasopressin come to the fore — the hormones of trust, calm and closeness. They are released during hugs and touch.
<b>Стресс, усталость, недосып.</b> Корти: Stress, fatigue, lack of sleep. Cortisol and anxiety suppress sex hormones and the reward system — desire decreases. It is also reduced by depression, some medications (antidepressants, hormonal drugs), thyroid disease, alcohol and high prolactin.
